title: Die Wergelder
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: An adult crime thriller by Hiroaki Samura set around a mysterious deal on a remote island that serves as a red-light district. A blonde sniper and an assassin in a Chinese dress clash, a group of misfit yakuza blunders in while trying to learn what is being traded, and at the center is a woman who was gravely wronged and is set on revenge. The title refers to the Germanic legal payment a killer's family owed the victim's family.
life_message: A grave wrong demands a price, and those who were wronged seek to collect it themselves.

content.note: Gunfights, martial-arts killings, gore and torture (AniList Gore, MU Blood and Gore/Torture, MangaDex Gore); publisher warns adult content, not for under 18.
Sustained menace, cult and cannibalism tags (AniList, spoiler-flagged), revenge thriller tone.
Frequent nudity, prostitution, bondage and sexual violence including rape in the backstory (AniList, MU Adult/Borderline H, MangaDex erotica + Sexual Violence); publisher 18+ warning.
Yakuza and criminal milieu suggests rough language; not documented (to verify).
Red-light district setting; drug or alcohol use not documented (to verify).
Central woman driven by severe trauma from sexual abuse (publisher blurb 'wronged in the worst imaginable ways'; MU Sexual Abuse).
Assassination and private revenge as the story's engine (publisher blurb; AniList Assassins/Revenge).

dominant: Revenge and retribution; criminal underworld power; exploitation of women

Dignity vs honor.evidence: A grave wrong must be answered personally; revenge drives the plot.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Lawless island run by criminals; no lawful order.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Yakuza group loyalty and personal grievance over civic law.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Crime hierarchies, but characters act on their own.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: No religious framework; a secular underworld.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival in a violent underworld comes first.

folkways.japan: Yakuza group loyalty and honor codes appear as genre conventions of Japanese crime fiction rather than as values the story argues for.

delivery.evidence: Publisher and database summaries present a revenge thriller with no stated thesis (to verify).
delivery.note: Summaries describe a revenge action thriller whose view of retribution is carried by events rather than speeches.

winners_losers: The story follows the wronged woman's revenge with sympathy; traffickers and abusers are the targets, and lawful justice is absent.
